scenario: A long-time budget-LCD phone user mainly reads, messages, scrolls social feeds, and occasionally watches video outdoors. A friend claims a flagship is worth the premium for its screen alone. The available material includes LCD and OLED mechanism references, definitions and boundaries for refresh rate, luminance, contrast, and viewing-distance-dependent pixel density, four price-separated catalog snapshots, and community discussions with conflicting or short-lived display experiences.
target: Explain the LCD and OLED mechanism difference without turning panel type into a universal winner. Distinguish the measurable display properties and the conditions under which they matter, compare the four frozen listing snapshots and their configuration caveats, and reconcile conflicting community experiences. Produce a person-specific test and stopping process for reading, messaging, scrolling, occasional video, outdoor visibility, comfort, and whole-phone tradeoffs, while stating that the material cannot prove a universal price-to-quality curve or stopping price.
